statement: Whenever the function returns a result ans, the following holds. Let A^0 = nums, and for t = 0,...,m-1 let A^{t+1} be A^t if queries[t][0] = 1, and otherwise let A^{t+1} be the array obtained from A^t by setting position queries[t][1] to queries[t][2] and leaving all other positions unchanged. Then len(ans) equals the number of t with 0 <= t < m and queries[t][0] = 1. For each p with 0 <= p < len(ans), let t be the p-th index (0-based, in increasing order) such that queries[t][0] = 1, and write queries[t] = [1, ql, qr]. Then ans[p] is exactly the number of integers k with ql < k < qr and A^t[k] > A^t[k-1] and A^t[k] > A^t[k+1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and m = len(queries). All indices are 0-based. 3 <= n <= 10^5. 1 <= m <= 10^5. For every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= nums[k] <= 10^5. For every i with 0 <= i < m: len(queries[i]) = 3; queries[i][0] is 1 or 2; if queries[i][0] = 1 then 0 <= queries[i][1] <= queries[i][2] <= n-1; if queries[i][0] = 2 then 0 <= queries[i][1] <= n-1 and 1 <= queries[i][2] <= 10^5.
